key_insight: Detonation-spraying parameters can tune the roughness, thickness, and hydrophobicity of titanium-dioxide-based metal–ceramic coatings.
engineering_relevance: The reported relationships could help select spraying conditions for coatings with greater hydrophobicity and controlled surface geometry.
method: Examine coating properties under varied detonation-spraying conditions.
Relate surface roughness and coating thickness to nozzle passage speed.
Model roughness and contact angle versus spray distance to identify hydrophobicity-maximizing conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports inverse-power relationships with nozzle passage speed and parabolic relationships with spray distance, but provides no numerical results or validation metrics.
watch_item: The operating ranges and optimal parameter values are absent from the abstract, limiting direct implementation of the predictive equations.
paper_title: Surface Characteristics of Titanium Based Coatings Obtained by Detonation Spraying Under Various Process Conditions
